Alex Chen: Heads-up — seeing a p99 latency jump on the canary GPU pool starting 06:12 UTC (~2x). Happens across short-seq traffic (<=128). Noticed around the driver rollout window. Logs point to heavy prefetch activity then KV evictions. :eyes:
Mia Patel: Where are you seeing the spike? per-model or global?
Alex Chen: Per-model on small-seq-heavy routes (chat-short), overall throughput steady but tail up. Attached sampling from console: `route=chat-short, model=rwd-base-7b, p50=18ms, p95=120ms, p99=420ms (normal ~200ms)`
Samir Rao: Can you paste the perf profile? curious about kernel launches + cudaMemcpy patterns.
Alex Chen: pasting a trimmed perf sample:
```
TIME 06:12:34 host gpu0 kernel Launch flash_attn_forward
cpu wait 12ms
cudaMemcpyAsync(prefetch) 8ms
KV cache evict loop 45ms
triton autoselect: chosen=fused_flash  (fallbacks seen)
```
Irina Volk: Hmm Triton autoselect changed heuristics in 535.86 driver — we saw different kernel fingerprinting earlier. Could be the selector choosing a prefetch-heavy kernel for short seqs.
Raul Gomez: Is this noisy neighbor (one tenant causing prefetch storms) or selector oscillation? Any single tenant showing high prefetch counters?
Alex Chen: Initial sampling: multiple tenants spiking prefetch RPCs concurrently, not single tenant. Prefetch throttle counter in runtime shows many small requests issuing prefetch on every request instead of cached KV hits.
Mia Patel: That smells like a batching/prefetch heuristic regression — maybe cache key miss policy changed. Did any rollout touch the KV allocator or prefetch TTL?
Samir Rao: I ran a micro-repro on a canary VM: toggling `PREFETCH_STRICT=1` (force prefix cache reuse) drops p99 back to baseline. With default heuristic we see repeated `cudaMemcpyAsync` + kernel launch churn.
Irina Volk: If `PREFETCH_STRICT` helps, selector is picking a kernel variant that expects cold KV (so it prefetches aggressively). Driver changes can alter memory residency behavior making prefetch costlier.
Raul Gomez: Steps to reproduce from my side?
Alex Chen: repro script (short):
```
# quick repro
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://canary/rwd-gen -d '{"input":"short prompt"}' &
done
# measure p99 from console
```
Run it with two parallel tenants at ~200rps each.
Mia Patel: Can we try a canary rollback to pre-driver or force Triton kernel override to previous fused_flash_revA to confirm?
Irina Volk: I can push a kernel pin on the canary group (override autoselect to fused_flash_revA) and flip it back if it doesn't help. Planning to schedule at 06:55 UTC.
deploy-bot: deploy: kernel-override/fused_flash_revA scheduled at 06:55:00 UTC by Irina Volk. ID: d-20260318-01
Samir Rao: I also grabbed nvprof traces — attaching short excerpt (top ops):
```
%Time  Kernel                   Calls   Avg ms
34.2  flash_attn_forward         1200    0.45
22.1  cudaMemcpyAsync(prefetch) 1200    0.37
13.7  kv_eviction_loop           200     0.95
```
With override, memcpy drops to ~0.12ms and kv_eviction_loop count halves.
Alex Chen: Great — if pin drops memcpy and evictions, likely kernel choice triggers redundant prefetch requests.
Raul Gomez: If we confirm, next steps: 1) roll pin to stable on canary pool, 2) create a selector test that runs across driver versions, 3) add an agressive caching flag to reduce prefetch chatter for short seqs.
Mia Patel: Also add a metric for "prefetch-to-kv_hit_ratio" so we can alert earlier.
Irina Volk: Doing the kernel pin now. Will report back in 10m.
Alex Chen: Thanks — leaving perf traces running. :thumbsup:
Irina Volk: Update @channel: pinned to fused_flash_revA on canary — initial observation after 5m: p99 back to ~210ms. Noisy prefetch counters down 78%. Rolling to more canaries in 15m if stable.
Samir Rao: Logs look clear. I'll open a perf regression ticket and attach traces + nvprof.
Raul Gomez: Filing infra follow-up to make Triton autoselect deterministic across driver minor versions.
Mia Patel: Nice work team. Keep monitoring for oscillations when we expand rollout. :rocket:
